2027-05-02.title: Fifth Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: The Spirit of truth will guide you
Rejoice before the Lord at the feast of weeks
David becomes great, for the Lord was with him
Filled with joy and the Holy Spirit
Seek the things that are above
Your pain will turn into joy
2027-05-02.alt: Season of Qyomtho. The Ascension of our Lord (Suloko) is on Thursday 6 May: remind the faithful.
2027-05-02.verse: So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
theo: At the Last Supper Jesus prepares his disciples for his going. “A little while, and you will no longer see me, and again a little while, and you will see me.” They will weep while the world rejoices, “but your pain will turn into joy.” He compares it to a woman in labour: her pain is forgotten in the joy of a child born into the world. The Resurrection is that birth; Christian joy is born through the Cross.

“So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.” This is the joy of Qyomtho: not a mood that changes with circumstances, but a gift no one can take away, because it rests on the risen Christ. Acts shows the first disciples, even when expelled from a city, “filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit”.

Jesus promises the Spirit: “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.” As the Ascension and Pentecost approach, the Church is taught to live not by sight but by the Spirit, who leads her into the fullness of truth. And Jesus teaches us to pray with confidence: “Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.”

St Paul gives the practical consequence: “If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above… Set your minds on things that are above.” Then he lists what must be put to death and what put on. Proverbs adds: “Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offences.” Easter joy shows itself in a changed life.
conn: The feast of weeks.
Deuteronomy 16:10–12: Israel rejoiced fifty days after Passover; Christians count fifty days from Easter to Pentecost.
Labour pains and new birth.
Isaiah 26:17–19 and 66:7–14 speak of birth pangs leading to new life; Jesus applies the image to his Passion and Resurrection.
Joy that cannot be taken.
Acts 13:52: persecution cannot remove the joy of the Spirit.
Things above.
Colossians 3:1: the risen life orients us towards Christ seated at the right hand of God.
altar: “I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice.” Every Holy Qurbono is this seeing again: the risen Lord comes, and our sorrow is turned into joy.
outline: The woman in labour: joy through the Cross.
Point 2 · Joy no one can take
Easter joy rests on Christ, not circumstances.
Preparing for the Ascension and Pentecost.
A changed life is the sign of Easter joy.
“No one will take your joy from you.”
live: Count your joys
Each evening this week, thank God for three joys of the day.
Ask in his name (John 16:24)
Bring one need to the Father with confidence in Jesus' name.
Come for the Ascension
Attend the Holy Qurbono of the Ascension on Thursday.
fathers: St Augustine
That little while seems long to us while it lasts; when it is over we shall know how little it was. Our joy is now in hope, then it will be in reality (Tractates on John 101).
St Cyril of Alexandria
The pain of the disciples was turned into joy when they saw the Lord risen; so too for us the sufferings of this world will be followed by the joy that no one can take away (Commentary on John 11).
magis: Evangelii Gaudium 1, 6
The joy of the Gospel fills the hearts of those who encounter Jesus; there are Christians whose lives seem like Lent without Easter.
Catechism 1829, 1832
Joy is a fruit of charity and of the Holy Spirit.
Catechism 243, 729
Christ promises the Spirit of truth who will guide the Church into all truth.
saints: Thursday 6 May: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord; Holy Qurbono for the people. The ten days of prayer for the coming of the Spirit begin.
2027-05-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you promised that our pain would turn into joy and that no one would take it from us. Send us your Spirit of truth, teach us to ask in your name, and set our hearts on the things that are above, where you are seated at the right hand of the Father. Amen.

2027-05-06.title: Suloko · The Ascension of our Lord
readings: The tablets placed in the ark
Elijah taken up; Elisha takes his mantle
I will write my law on their hearts
He was lifted up, and a cloud took him
He blessed them and was carried up into heaven
2027-05-06.alt: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord: Holy Qurbono for the people. Ten days of prayer for the coming of the Holy Spirit follow; according to the lectionary, marriages are not celebrated in these days.
2027-05-06.verse: While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
theo: Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany, “and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.” The last earthly sight of Jesus is of hands raised in blessing. He goes, but he does not stop blessing his Church.

The Ascension is not Jesus leaving us; it is our humanity entering heaven. The Son of God, who took our flesh, now takes it to the right hand of the Father. St Mark says: “he was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.” Where the Head has gone, the body hopes to follow. Our true home is with him.

The angels ask the disciples: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven? This Jesus… will come in the same way as you saw him go.” The Ascension is not a time for gazing at the sky but for mission: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation… And they went out and proclaimed the good news everywhere, while the Lord worked with them.”

As Elijah was taken up and Elisha received his mantle and spirit, so Christ ascends and pours out his Spirit on his Church. Jeremiah's promise will be fulfilled at Pentecost: “I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts.” Like the disciples, who “returned to Jerusalem with great joy and were continually in the temple blessing God”, we now enter ten days of prayer for the Spirit.
conn: Elijah's mantle.
2 Kings 2:13–15: Elisha takes the mantle of the ascended Elijah and receives his spirit: a figure of the Church receiving Christ's Spirit.
The ark and the law.
Deuteronomy 10:1–5: the tablets placed in the ark; Jeremiah 31:33: the law written on hearts by the Spirit.
Gifts from on high.
Ephesians 4:8–11: the ascended Christ gives apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to build up his body.
A light to the nations.
Isaiah 49:6 and Acts 1:8: the mission goes to the ends of the earth.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono we are invited: “Lift up your hearts”, and we answer, “They are with the Lord.” The ascended Christ, seated at the Father's right hand, comes down to us on the altar, and lifts us up to him.
outline: Hands raised in blessing: the last sight of Jesus.
Where the Head has gone, the body will follow.
The Spirit given to the Church.
With Mary and the apostles, waiting for Pentecost.
live: Keep the ten days
Pray each day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit.”
Go and tell (Mark 16:15)
Share the Good News with one person this week, in word or deed.
Lift up your heart
At the Qurbono, really lift up your heart to the Lord at “Lift up your hearts”.
fathers: St Leo the Great
“Christ's Ascension is our elevation; where the glory of the Head has gone before, there the hope of the body is called to follow” (Sermon 73 on the Ascension, 4).
St Augustine

“Today our Lord Jesus Christ ascended into heaven; let our hearts ascend with him… He did not leave heaven when he came down to us; nor did he withdraw from us when he went up again into heaven” (Sermon on the Ascension, Mai 98).
magis: Catechism 659–667
Christ's Ascension marks the definitive entrance of Jesus' humanity into God's heavenly domain; he precedes us so that we might live in hope of following.
Catechism 1137–1139
The heavenly liturgy: the ascended Christ is the high priest of the true sanctuary.
Catechism 2623
The disciples, with Mary, persevered in prayer awaiting the Spirit.
saints: Sunday 9 May: VI Sunday after Qyomtho. Sunday 16 May: Pentecost.
2027-05-06.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, ascended into heaven, you raised your hands to bless your disciples and took our humanity to the Father's right hand. Bless us from heaven, lift up our hearts to you, send us to proclaim your Gospel, and pour out your Spirit on your Church. Amen.

2027-05-09.title: Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: I am the Lord; I will free you
Your immortal spirit is in all things
I have swept away your sins like a cloud
The eyes of your heart enlightened
It is to your advantage that I go away
2027-05-09.alt: Sunday between the Ascension and Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary this was Social Communication Media Day. Remind the faithful about Pentecost next Sunday.
2027-05-09.verse: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
theo: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church lives in the upper room. The apostles, “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus”, are “constantly devoting themselves to prayer.” Jesus has gone to the Father; the Spirit has not yet come. It is a time of waiting, but not of emptiness: it is the Church at prayer, gathered around Mary.

Jesus had told them: “It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.” His physical presence was limited to one place; the Spirit will make him present everywhere, in every heart and every altar. The Spirit “will prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment”: he convicts, converts and gives courage.

In the evening Gospel we hear the beginning of Jesus' great priestly prayer: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you… And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” The ascended Christ continues this prayer for us at the Father's right hand.

God says to Joshua as he takes up Moses' task: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.” St Paul prays that “with the eyes of your heart enlightened, you may know what is the hope to which he has called you.” Let us spend this week like the apostles: in prayer, with Mary, waiting for the Spirit.
conn: The upper room.
The room of the Last Supper becomes the room of waiting and of Pentecost (Acts 1:13; 2:1).
Mary at prayer.
Mary, overshadowed by the Spirit at the Annunciation, prays with the Church for the Spirit's coming (Acts 1:14).
Joshua after Moses.
As Joshua received Moses' charge, the apostles receive Christ's mission; the same promise: “I will be with you.”
Sins swept away.
Isaiah 44:22: the forgiveness the Spirit brings when he convicts the world of sin.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono the Church does what the apostles did in the upper room: gathered with Mary and the saints, she prays for the Spirit, and the Spirit comes upon the gifts and upon us.
outline: The Spirit makes Christ present everywhere.
The Church at prayer with Mary.
Point 4 · Eternal life is to know God
live: A Pentecost novena
Pray each day until Pentecost for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
Pray with Mary
Pray the Rosary this week with the intention of a new Pentecost in your family.
Use media well
Share something good and true online this week; avoid sharing gossip or anger.
fathers: St Augustine

It was expedient for them that the form of a servant be taken from their sight, so that, no longer clinging to the flesh, they might love him spiritually and receive the Spirit (Tractates on John 94).
St Cyril of Alexandria
Christ had to depart in the flesh so that the Spirit might dwell in us; through the Spirit Christ himself is with us (Commentary on John 10).
magis: Catechism 729–730
Only when the hour of his glorification had come did Jesus promise the coming of the Spirit; the Spirit will be with us for ever.
Catechism 726
Mary, filled with the Holy Spirit, is present with the apostles at the dawn of the last times.
Inter Mirifica 3 / Aetatis Novae
The Church sees the means of social communication as gifts of God to be used for the good.
saints: The days of prayer for the Holy Spirit continue. Sunday 16 May: Pentecost.
2027-05-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, you went to the Father so that the Advocate might come. Gather us with Mary and the apostles in prayer, make us strong and courageous, enlighten the eyes of our hearts, and send your Holy Spirit upon your Church. Amen.

2027-05-16.title: The Sunday of Pentecost
readings: The Advocate will teach you everything
The spirit rests on the seventy elders
The land divided among the tribes
The spirit of God comes upon Saul
A new heart and a new spirit
Varieties of gifts, the same Spirit
Another Advocate, to be with you for ever
2027-05-16.alt: The Sunday of Pentecost: Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Pentecost begins.
2027-05-16.verse: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.
theo: “When the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place. And suddenly from heaven there came a sound like the rush of a violent wind… Divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit.” Fifty days after Easter, the promise of the Father is fulfilled. The Church, gathered in prayer with Mary, receives the Spirit and is born into mission.

The crowds from every nation hear the apostles “in our own languages… speaking about God's deeds of power.” At Babel human pride scattered the nations in confusion of tongues; at Pentecost the Spirit gathers them in one faith, each hearing in his own language. The Church is catholic from her first day: one Spirit, many peoples, many languages, including ours.

The Old Testament readings were longing for this day. Moses wished: “Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!” Ezekiel promised: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you… I will put my spirit within you.” Now it happens. The Spirit who rested on a few prophets is poured out on all the baptised.

Jesus had promised: “I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever… I will not leave you orphaned.” St Paul explains that the one Spirit gives many gifts, “to each… for the common good.” Each of us received this Spirit in Baptism and Chrismation. Pentecost asks: are we living by the Spirit's power, or as if he had never come?
conn: Babel reversed.
Genesis 11: one language divided by pride; Acts 2: many languages united in praise.
Sinai and Pentecost.
Pentecost was the feast of the giving of the Law at Sinai; now the Law is written on hearts by the Spirit (Jeremiah 31:33; Ezekiel 36:27).
The seventy elders.
Numbers 11: the spirit shared from Moses to the elders; Pentecost: the Spirit given to the whole Church.
Fire.
The burning bush, the pillar of fire, the coal of Isaiah: now tongues of fire on each disciple.
altar: At the epiclesis of every Holy Qurbono the priest calls the Holy Spirit upon the bread and wine and upon the people. Every Qurbono is a little Pentecost: the same Spirit who came upon the apostles makes Christ present and makes us one body.
outline: Wind and fire in the upper room.
Another Advocate, for ever: we are not orphans.
One Spirit, many languages: the Church for all nations.
Ezekiel and Moses: the Spirit poured on all.
Point 4 · Gifts for the common good
Discover and use your gifts in the Church.
“Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.”
live: Renew your Chrismation
Thank God for the Spirit received with holy Myron at Baptism; pray “Come, Holy Spirit” daily.
Use one gift
Offer one gift you have (music, teaching, care, skill) to your parish this month.
Speak the language of love
Be reconciled with someone with whom you “don't speak the same language”.
fathers: St Irenaeus of Lyons

The Spirit descended at Pentecost, having power to admit all nations to life; he brought the scattered tribes to unity and offered to the Father the first fruits of all nations (Against Heresies III, 17, 2).
St Cyril of Jerusalem
The Spirit comes gently, like rain on dry ground; one water becomes the lily's whiteness and the rose's red; so the one Spirit works in each as he wills (Catechetical Lectures 16, 12).
magis: Catechism 731–732
On the day of Pentecost the Passover of Christ is fulfilled in the outpouring of the Holy Spirit; the Holy Trinity is fully revealed.
Catechism 1287–1288
The Spirit given at Pentecost is communicated to the baptised through the sacrament of Chrismation (Confirmation).
Catechism 799–801
Charisms are graces of the Spirit for the building up of the Church.
saints: Friday 21 May: Golden Friday (Acts 3:1–10, the healing at the Beautiful Gate). 26 May: St Philip Neri.
2027-05-16.prayer: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. As you came upon the apostles with Mary, come upon our families, our parish and our Church: give us a new heart, unite us in one faith, and send us to proclaim the wonders of God. Amen.

2027-05-23.title: First Sunday after Pentecost
readings: The manna ceases; they eat the produce of the land
Filled with the spirit of the Lord
Plans for your welfare, a future with hope
The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily
2027-05-23.alt: Season of Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Vocation Day.
2027-05-23.verse: By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
theo: The season of Pentecost is the season of the Church's life in the Spirit. If Pentecost was the planting, these Sundays are about the fruit. St Paul names it: “the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control… If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.”

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells the parable of the sower. Seed falls on the path, on rock, among thorns and on good soil. “As for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.” The Spirit sows; we must become good soil: attentive, deep, free from the thorns of worry and riches.

In the Gospel the crowds follow Jesus after the multiplication of loaves, looking for more bread. He tells them: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.” When they ask what work God wants, he answers: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.” “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” Israel's manna stopped when they reached the promised land; the true Bread will never fail.

Jeremiah gives a word of hope to people in exile: “I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope… When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart.” God has a plan, a vocation, for each of us; the Spirit leads us to discover it.
conn: Manna and the land.
Joshua 5:12: the manna ceased when Israel ate the produce of the land; Jesus is the true bread from heaven (John 6:32–33).
The Exodus.
Exodus 12: God's people go out from slavery; the Spirit leads us from the slavery of the flesh to freedom (Galatians 5:16–18).
The Bereans.
Acts 17:11: they examined the Scriptures daily; the good soil is a heart that studies the Word.
Filled with the spirit.
Micah 3:8: the prophet filled with the spirit of the Lord to speak truth.
altar: “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” In the Holy Qurbono we receive the bread that endures for eternal life, and the Spirit makes us bear fruit.
outline: Point 1 · The fruit of the Spirit
Love, joy, peace… a portrait of Christ in us.
The sower: hearing, holding fast, patient endurance.
Work for the food of eternal life.
Vocation Day: God's plan for each life.
“If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.”
live: Choose one fruit
Pick one fruit of the Spirit (patience, kindness…) to practise deliberately this week.
Read the Word daily (Acts 17:11)
Like the Bereans, read a short passage of Scripture each day.
Pray for vocations
Pray for young people discerning priesthood, religious life or marriage.
fathers: St Augustine
Be good soil: do not let the Word fall on the path of a careless heart, on the rock of a hard heart, or among the thorns of worldly cares (Sermon 73).
St John Chrysostom
The fruit of the Spirit is not something we produce alone; the Spirit works in us, but we must cooperate, as soil receives rain and bears grain (Commentary on Galatians 5).
magis: Catechism 1832
The fruits of the Spirit are perfections that the Holy Spirit forms in us as the first fruits of eternal glory.
Catechism 2707–2708
Meditation on the Word; the parable of the sower.
Catechism 1533–1535
Vocations to marriage and the ordained ministry at the service of communion.
saints: 26 May: St Philip Neri. Weekdays of the season of Pentecost.
2027-05-23.prayer: Holy Spirit, sower of the Word, make our hearts good soil. Bear in us the fruit of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control; feed us with the bread from heaven, and show each of us the plan you have for our lives. Amen.

2027-05-30.title: Second Sunday after Pentecost
readings: You shall be holy, for I am holy
David becomes king over all Israel
The exiles weep, fast and pray
The living God, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed
I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh
No condemnation for those in Christ Jesus
Whoever loses his life for my sake will find it
2027-05-30.verse: Whoever does not take up the cross and follow me is not worthy of me. Those who find their life will lose it, and those who lose their life for my sake will find it.
theo: On the morning of Pentecost Peter stands up and explains what the crowds are seeing: it is the fulfilment of Joel: “In the last days it will be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy… Then everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” The Spirit is not reserved to a few; he is poured out on young and old, men and women, all who call on the Lord.

St Paul tells us what this means for daily life: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death… If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies also through his Spirit that dwells in you.” The Spirit who raised Jesus lives in us.

In the evening Gospel Jesus spends the night in prayer on the mountain, then chooses the Twelve and proclaims: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.” The Beatitudes are the portrait of a life led by the Spirit, often hidden, often poor, always blessed.

Leviticus gives the deepest command: “You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.” Jesus shows the way: “Whoever does not take up the cross and follow me is not worthy of me… whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones in the name of a disciple… none of these will lose their reward.” Holiness is the Cross carried with love, and the small cup of water given in Christ's name.
conn: Holiness.
Leviticus 19:2: “You shall be holy”; the Spirit is the Holy Spirit, who makes us holy (Romans 8:9–11).
David the king.
2 Samuel 5: the shepherd-king; Jesus, Son of David, chooses the Twelve as shepherds for the new Israel (Luke 6:13).
Daniel's God.
Daniel 6:26: the living God whose kingdom shall never be destroyed; the kingdom Jesus promises to the poor.
Exiles who pray.
Baruch 1:5: the exiles weep, fast and pray; “blessed are you who weep now.”
altar: Jesus prayed all night before choosing the Twelve. Every Holy Qurbono is offered by the Church built on the apostles; the Spirit who raised Jesus gives life to us through the Body and Blood of the Lord.
outline: After Pentecost: the Spirit for all flesh.
The Spirit of life sets us free.
The Beatitudes as the life of the Spirit.
Point 4 · The cross and the cup of water
“You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
live: A cup of cold water
Do one small, hidden act of kindness each day this week in Jesus' name.
Pray before decisions
Like Jesus before choosing the Twelve, pray before an important decision.
Call on the Lord
Repeat during the day: “Lord Jesus, have mercy on me.”
fathers: St Ambrose
Luke places poverty first among the beatitudes, for it is the mother of the virtues; whoever despises the world's goods is ready to receive the kingdom (Exposition of Luke 5, 50–53).
St Augustine
The law of the Spirit of life is love poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us (On the Spirit and the Letter 17, 29).
magis: Catechism 1716–1717
The Beatitudes depict the countenance of Jesus Christ and portray his charity.
Catechism 2012–2013
All Christians are called to holiness and the perfection of charity.
Lumen Gentium 40
The Lord Jesus preached holiness of life to each and every one of his disciples.
saints: Weekdays of the season of Pentecost. Sunday 6 June: III Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-05-30.prayer: Spirit of life, poured out on all flesh, set us free from sin and death and make us holy as the Father is holy. Teach us the joy of the Beatitudes, give us strength to carry the cross, and let no cup of water given in Christ's name be forgotten. Amen.

quick: “Your pain will turn into joy”: Easter joy is born through the Cross.
No one can take away the joy that rests on the risen Christ.
The Spirit of truth will guide us into all truth.
2027-05-02.action: Each evening this week thank God for three joys of the day.
2027-05-02.question: What steals my joy, and how can Christ give it back?
2027-05-02.special: Fifth Sunday after Qyomtho. Announce Suloko (Ascension) on Thursday 6 May.
illus: In a Kerala hospital a young mother, exhausted after a long labour, holds her newborn and smiles: “I've forgotten all the pain.” Jesus used exactly this picture for the joy of Easter.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends they would be sad when he died, but their sadness would turn into joy when they saw him again. And nobody can take that joy away!
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad, that they may find joy in Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What made each of us happy this week? Let's thank God.”

kidsaint: A bishop of Alexandria who bravely taught that Jesus is truly God, even when he was sent away from his city five times. Lesson: stay true to Jesus even when it is hard.
term: From Qyomtho to Pentecost the Church keeps fifty days of Easter joy, like Israel's fifty days from Passover to the feast of weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9–12).
termMore: Jesus' name for the Holy Spirit in John (14:17; 16:13): the Spirit who leads the Church into the fullness of truth.

quick: Jesus ascends with hands raised in blessing.
Our humanity has entered heaven: where the Head is, the body hopes to follow.
Not gazing upwards, but going out: the Ascension leads to mission.
2027-05-06.action: Pray every day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit.”
2027-05-06.question: Is my heart lifted up to the Lord, or only looking at earthly things?
2027-05-06.special: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. Ten days of prayer until Pentecost (no marriage celebrations, as in the lectionary).
illus: When a Kerala father leaves for work abroad, the family gathers at the door and he raises his hand to bless the children before the car leaves. They remember that blessing for months. Jesus left his disciples with his hands raised in blessing, and he has never lowered them.

family.explain: Forty days after Easter, Jesus blessed his friends and went up to heaven. He is with God the Father, and he still blesses us. He promised to send the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for families separated by work abroad, and for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we pray together for the Holy Spirit these ten days?”

kidsaint: When his teacher Elijah was taken up to heaven, Elisha picked up his cloak and received his spirit to carry on God's work. Lesson: when Jesus went to heaven, he gave us his Spirit to continue his work.
term: Syriac for “ascension”: the feast of the Ascension of our Lord, forty days after Qyomtho, always on a Thursday.
termMore: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church prays, like the apostles with Mary in the upper room (Acts 1:14), for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

quick: “It is to your advantage that I go away”: the Spirit will make Christ present everywhere.
The Church waits in prayer with Mary.
“Be strong and courageous; the Lord is with you.”
2027-05-09.action: Pray each day until Pentecost for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-09.question: Which gift of the Holy Spirit do I most need?
2027-05-09.special: Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho. Announce Pentecost next Sunday. (In 2025–26 also Social Communication Media Day; check the collection.)
illus: Before a big family wedding in Kerala, relatives gather in the house days earlier to pray the Rosary each evening. The house becomes an upper room. That is what the Church does between the Ascension and Pentecost.

family.explain: After Jesus went to heaven, his friends prayed together with Mary, waiting for the Holy Spirit Jesus had promised.
family.intention: We pray for the gifts of the Holy Spirit for each of us.
family.ask: Ask: “Which gift of the Spirit do we need most in our family?”

catechism: The gifts of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: After Jesus went to heaven, Mary prayed with the apostles, waiting for the Holy Spirit. She is the Mother of the Church. Lesson: pray with Mary, and the Spirit will come.
term: In the 2025–26 lectionary the Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho was Social Communication Media Day, when the Church prays for the right use of the media.
termMore: John 17, the prayer of Jesus to the Father at the Last Supper, is called his “high-priestly prayer”: for his glory, for his disciples, and for all who will believe.

quick: Pentecost: the Spirit comes as wind and fire; the Church is born into mission.
Babel reversed: one Spirit, many languages, all nations.
A new heart and a new spirit: the Spirit is poured on all the baptised.
2027-05-16.action: Offer one of your gifts to the service of your parish this month.
2027-05-16.question: Am I living by the power of the Holy Spirit, or as if he had never come?
2027-05-16.special: The Sunday of Pentecost: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Pentecost begins.
illus: At a Kerala charismatic retreat centre, people from every state of India pray together in Malayalam, Tamil, Hindi, Konkani and English, and yet it feels like one prayer. That is Pentecost: one Spirit, many tongues.

family.explain: On Pentecost the Holy Spirit came on the apostles like a strong wind and tongues of fire. They became brave and told everyone about Jesus in many languages!
family.intention: We pray for the Holy Spirit to fill our family with love and courage.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift has God given each of us to help others?”

catechism: Chrismation and the gift of the Spirit.
kidsaint: A joyful priest of Rome who loved the Holy Spirit and made young people laugh while teaching them to pray. People called him the apostle of Rome. Lesson: the Holy Spirit gives joy.
term: Greek for “fiftieth”: the fiftieth day after Qyomtho, when the Holy Spirit came upon the apostles and Mary (Acts 2). In the West Syriac tradition the Pentecost service includes solemn prayers on bended knee for the gift of the Spirit.
termMore: The fifth season of the Syro-Malankara year, from Pentecost until the Transfiguration season: the time of the Church's mission in the power of the Spirit.

quick: After Pentecost: the Spirit bears fruit in us.
Be good soil: hear the Word, hold it fast, bear fruit with patience.
Work for the bread that endures: believe in the One God has sent.
2027-05-23.action: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately this week.
2027-05-23.question: What kind of soil is my heart for God's Word?
2027-05-23.special: First Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26 also Vocation Day; check the collection.)
illus: Kerala farmers know that seed sown on laterite rock dries up, while the same seed in the paddy field brings a harvest. The difference is the soil, not the seed. The Spirit sows the same Word in all of us.

family.explain: The Holy Spirit helps good things grow in us, like fruit on a tree: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
family.intention: We pray that the fruit of the Spirit may grow in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Which fruit of the Spirit will each of us practise this week?”

kidsaint: A Syro-Malabar sister from Thrissur who visited poor families, cared for the sick and the dying, and founded the Congregation of the Holy Family. The fruit of the Spirit was seen in her kindness. Lesson: let your kindness show God's love.
term: The season after Pentecost when the Church, filled with the Spirit, grows and bears fruit. In the Syro-Malankara year it leads into the season of the Transfiguration.
termMore: The Friday after Pentecost, when the lectionary reads the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk” (Acts 3:6).

quick: The Spirit is poured out on all who call on the Lord.
“No condemnation for those in Christ Jesus”: the Spirit gives life.
“Be holy”: the cross carried with love and the cup of water given in his name.
2027-05-30.action: Do one small, hidden act of kindness each day this week in Jesus' name.
2027-05-30.question: Which beatitude is God asking me to live now?
illus: In many Kerala homes a pot of water is kept by the gate in summer for anyone passing by. No one sees who fills it. Jesus says not even that cup of water will lose its reward.

family.explain: Jesus says even giving a cup of water to someone in his name is precious to God. Small kindnesses matter!
family.intention: We pray to be holy and kind, as God is holy.
family.ask: Ask: “What small kindness can each of us do this week?”

kidsaint: Jesus prayed all night and then chose twelve ordinary men: fishermen, a tax collector and others. With the Holy Spirit they carried the Gospel to the whole world, and St Thomas came to India. Lesson: God chooses ordinary people for great things.
term: The blessings with which Jesus begins his teaching (Matthew 5; Luke 6). Luke gives four blessings and four woes. They describe the happiness of those who belong to God's kingdom.
termMore: After Pentecost the lectionary reads how the Spirit forms the Church: the apostles' preaching in Acts, Paul's teaching on life in the Spirit, and Jesus' calling and sending of disciples.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, at the Last Supper Jesus told his friends: “A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me.” They did not understand. He explained with a picture every mother knows: a woman in labour has pain, but when the child is born she forgets the pain for joy.

That is Easter. The Cross was the labour pain; the Resurrection is the birth of new life. And Jesus promised: “I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.” Christian joy is not the absence of trouble. It is a joy that rests on the risen Christ, and so no one can take it away.

In Acts the disciples are thrown out of a city, and yet they are “filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.” Jesus also promises the Spirit of truth to guide us, and invites us to ask in his name, “so that your joy may be complete”. On Thursday we celebrate his Ascension; then we wait for the Spirit.

St Paul tells us how this joy shows: “Seek the things that are above.” Put off anger, lies and impurity; put on compassion and love. As Proverbs says, “love covers all offences.” Let us live this week as people whose joy no one can take away. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told his friends: “You will be sad for a little while, but then you will be very happy!”
They were sad when Jesus died, but so happy when they saw him alive again! Jesus said nobody can take that joy away.
When you feel sad, remember Jesus is alive and loves you. Let's say: “Jesus, you are my joy!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, forty days after Easter Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany. He lifts up his hands and blesses them, and while he is blessing them he is carried up into heaven. The last picture the disciples have of Jesus is of hands raised in blessing. He has never lowered them.

The Ascension does not mean that Jesus has gone far away. It means that our human nature, which he took from Mary, now sits at the right hand of the Father. Where he, our Head, has gone, we, his body, hope to follow. Heaven is our home.

But the angels say: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” The Ascension is not a time for gazing at the sky; it is a time for mission. Jesus said: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news.” And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them.

Elijah was taken up, and Elisha received his mantle and his spirit. Jesus ascends, and he will send his Spirit upon us at Pentecost. Like the apostles with Mary, let us spend these ten days in prayer: Come, Holy Spirit. And at every Qurbono, when we hear “Lift up your hearts,” let us truly lift them up to him. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus went up to heaven! He took his friends to a hill, raised his hands and blessed them, and then went up into the sky until a cloud hid him.
Jesus is now with God the Father, but he still blesses us and loves us. And he promised to send the Holy Spirit to help us.
For the next ten days, let's pray every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, we are living the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. Jesus has gone to the Father; the Spirit has not yet come. And what did the apostles do? They went to the upper room and “devoted themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus.”

Jesus had said something surprising: “It is to your advantage that I go away.” How can it be better that Jesus goes? Because when he was on earth he could be in one place at a time. The Spirit makes him present everywhere: in every heart, in every family, on every altar. The Spirit will convict the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment.

In the evening Gospel Jesus prays: “Father, the hour has come… This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” He is still praying for us at the right hand of the Father.

And God says to us what he said to Joshua: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.” This week let us do what the apostles did: pray with Mary, every day, “Come, Holy Spirit.” Amen.
kids: Children, after Jesus went back to heaven, his friends waited in a room in Jerusalem. What were they doing? Praying, together with Mary!
Jesus had promised to send the Holy Spirit to help them. Next Sunday we will celebrate when the Spirit came!
This week, let's pray with Mary every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the birthday of the Church. Fifty days after Easter, the apostles were gathered in prayer with Mary. Suddenly there came a sound like a mighty wind, and tongues like fire rested on each of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit, and the frightened men who had locked the doors went out into the streets and proclaimed Christ.

People from every nation heard them, each in his own language, speaking of the wonders of God. At Babel, pride had scattered humanity into many languages that could not understand one another. At Pentecost the Spirit gathers the nations into one faith, without erasing their languages. That is why we can pray the Holy Qurbono in Syriac and Malayalam, in Tamil and Hindi and English: one Spirit, many tongues.

Moses once said: “Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!” Ezekiel promised: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you.” Today it happens. And it happened to you on the day of your Baptism, when you were anointed with holy Myron. The Spirit is not only for bishops and saints; he lives in you.

St Paul says the one Spirit gives many gifts, each for the common good. What is your gift? Music, teaching, caring for the sick, organising, praying? Offer it. And let us pray today with the whole Church: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and kindle in us the fire of your love. Amen.
kids: Children, happy birthday to the Church! Today the Holy Spirit came on the apostles like a big wind and little flames of fire!
The apostles were afraid before, but the Spirit made them brave, and they told everyone about Jesus in many languages.
The same Holy Spirit came to you at your baptism. He helps you to be brave and kind. Let's pray: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we celebrated Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit. Today we ask: what difference does the Spirit make? St Paul answers: the Spirit bears fruit. “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.” Read that list slowly; it is a portrait of Jesus, and of what he wants to grow in us.

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells of a sower. Some seed falls on the path, some on rock, some among thorns, and some on good soil. The seed is the same; the soil makes the difference. The good soil is “an honest and good heart” that hears the Word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience. The Spirit keeps sowing; are we good soil?

In John's Gospel the crowds look for Jesus because he gave them bread. He tells them: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.” And he says: “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” That bread is given to us at this altar.

Today is also a day to pray for vocations. Jeremiah says: “I know the plans I have for you, plans for your welfare, to give you a future with hope.” God has a plan for every young person here: priesthood, religious life, marriage, a mission. Let us ask the Spirit to show it, and let us choose this week one fruit of the Spirit to practise. Amen.
kids: Children, when a tree is healthy, it gives fruit. When the Holy Spirit lives in us, we give fruit too: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness!
Jesus told a story about a farmer sowing seed. The seed that fell on good soil grew a big harvest. Our hearts should be good soil for God's Word.
Which fruit will you grow this week? Kindness? Patience? Let's say: “Holy Spirit, help me grow good fruit!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the day of Pentecost Peter stood up and said: this is what the prophet Joel foretold: “I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh… everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Not only on priests and prophets, but on sons and daughters, old and young. On you.

And what does the Spirit do in us? St Paul says: “There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. The law of the Spirit of life has set you free.” The same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead lives in us and will raise our mortal bodies. We are not slaves of sin; we are temples of the Spirit.

In the Gospel Jesus prays all night, chooses the Twelve, and then looks at his disciples and says: Blessed are you who are poor, blessed are you who are hungry, blessed are you who weep. This is the strange happiness of the Spirit: not the happiness of the rich and comfortable, but of those who trust God.

God says in Leviticus: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.” Holiness is not only for saints in pictures. Jesus shows two ways: to take up the cross and follow him, and to give a cup of cold water to a little one in his name. Big crosses and small kindnesses. Let us do one hidden act of kindness each day this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once prayed all night long! And in the morning he chose twelve friends to be his apostles.
Then he said: “Happy are the poor, happy are the hungry, happy are those who cry, because God will take care of them.”
Jesus also said that even giving a cup of water in his name is precious. What kind thing can you do today?

intro: Theme: “Your pain will turn into joy.”

Before his Passion Jesus prepared his disciples for sorrow, and promised a joy no one could take away. In the Easter season the Church hears these words as fulfilled, and learns that the Spirit of truth leads us into this joy.

sub: Jesus compares the disciples' grief to a mother in labour: pain that gives way to new life.
The Psalmist knew: weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
Easter joy does not deny suffering; it passes through it.
q: Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
points.apply: Offer one present sorrow to the Lord, trusting it will become joy.

sub: God's counsel is wonderful and his wisdom excellent.
Jesus promises the Spirit of truth who will guide us into all truth.
The Spirit speaks through Scripture and the teaching of the Church, never against them.
q: This also comes from the LORD of hosts; he is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.
points.apply: Before every decision this week, pray: “Come, Holy Spirit, guide me.”

sub: At the feast of Weeks all rejoiced together: children, servants, strangers, orphans and widows.
The first disciples, though persecuted, were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
Christian joy is never selfish; it includes the poor and the lonely.
q: Rejoice before the LORD your God—you and your sons and your daughters, your male and female slaves, the Levites resident in your towns, as well as the strangers, the orphans, and the widows who are among you.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Invite someone lonely to share a family meal or celebration.

concl: The Risen Lord gives a joy that the world cannot give or take away.
Let us ask in his name, let the Spirit guide us, and share our joy with all.
2027-05-02.resolve: Begin preparing for Pentecost: pray each day “Come, Holy Spirit.”

intro: Theme: “He was carried up into heaven, blessing them.”
Forty days after his Resurrection the Lord ascends. It is not a farewell of absence but of glory: our human nature, in Christ, enters heaven, and the Church is sent to the ends of the earth.

sub: Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind; Elisha received his spirit.
Jesus lifts up his hands and blesses the disciples; while blessing them he is carried up.
His last gesture on earth is blessing: his hands remain raised over the Church.
q: As they continued walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah ascended in a whirlwind into heaven.
Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
points.apply: Receive the final blessing at every Qurbono as Christ's own blessing.

points.h: Seated at the right hand of the Father
sub: The Psalm foretold: “Sit at my right hand.”
Christ, true God and true man, takes our humanity into the glory of the Father.
There he intercedes for us as our High Priest; where the Head has gone, the members hope to follow (CCC 661–667).
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Lift your heart to heaven each day: “Lord, draw me to where you are.”

points.h: Why stand looking up? Be witnesses
sub: The prophets saw that the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha.
The angels ask: “Why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” He will come again.
Meanwhile, with the power of the Spirit, we are witnesses to the ends of the earth.
q: When the company of prophets who were at Jericho saw him at a distance, they declared, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.”
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
points.apply: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit with Mary, from tomorrow until Pentecost.

concl: The Ascension is the feast of our hope: our humanity is in heaven with Christ.
Let us return like the apostles “with great joy”, praying with Mary for the Spirit.
2027-05-06.resolve: Pray the novena to the Holy Spirit from the Ascension to Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “Waiting for the Spirit with Mary.”

Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church waits in the upper room. Jesus has said it is better for us that he goes, for then the Advocate will come. His high-priestly prayer asks that we may all be one.

sub: The apostles, with Mary and the women, devote themselves to prayer.
Waiting is not idleness; it is opening the heart to God's gift.
God's spirit already fills all things; we pray that he fill us anew.
q: For your immortal spirit is in all things.
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary each day this week for a new Pentecost in your family.

points.h: Better for you that I go
sub: Jesus' bodily presence was in one place; the Spirit makes him present everywhere.
The Spirit convicts the world of sin, not to condemn but to heal.
Isaiah: God sweeps away our sins like mist and calls us back.
q: I have swept away your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like mist; return to me, for I have redeemed you.
It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you one sin to be healed, and confess it.

points.h: That they may all be one
sub: God promised: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.”
Jesus prays that his disciples be one as he and the Father are one.
Unity in families, parishes and among Christians is the Spirit's work and our task.
q: I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.
That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Heal one division before Pentecost: call, visit or forgive.

concl: The upper room teaches us to wait, pray and seek unity.
Let us prepare with Mary for the coming of the Spirit next Sunday.
2027-05-09.resolve: Pray daily until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.”

intro: Theme: “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit.”

Fifty days after Easter the promise of the Father is fulfilled. Wind and fire fill the upper room; frightened disciples become bold witnesses; people of many languages hear the wonders of God. The Church is born into mission.

points.h: A new heart and a new spirit
sub: Ezekiel promised a heart of flesh for a heart of stone, and God's own Spirit within.
At Pentecost the promise is fulfilled: wind fills the house, tongues of fire rest on each.
The same Spirit came upon us in Baptism and Chrismation with holy Myron.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. I will put my spirit within you.

Divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Chrismation, and ask the Spirit to rekindle its grace.

points.h: One Spirit for all God's people
sub: Moses longed that all the Lord's people be prophets.
At Pentecost the Spirit is given not to a few but to all, young and old, men and women.
Many languages hear one Gospel: Babel's division is healed in the Church.
q: Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!
In our own languages we hear them speaking about God's deeds of power.
points.apply: Use the gift the Spirit gave you (music, teaching, caring) in the service of your parish.

points.h: The Advocate who teaches and transforms
sub: When the Spirit came upon Saul, he was “turned into a different person”.
Jesus promised the Advocate who teaches everything and reminds us of his words.
The Spirit does not replace Christ; he makes Christ alive in us.
q: Then the spirit of the LORD will possess you … and be turned into a different person.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.
points.apply: Read one chapter of the Acts of the Apostles each day this week.

concl: Pentecost is the birthday of the Church and the fulfilment of Easter.
Let us live by the Spirit, speak the language of love, and bear witness to Christ everywhere.
2027-05-16.resolve: Pray each morning this week: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart and kindle in me the fire of your love.”

intro: Theme: “The Spirit bears fruit in good soil.”
After Pentecost the Church asks what difference the Spirit makes. The answer is fruit: a heart that receives the Word, a life that shows love and joy, and a people fed by the bread that endures.

sub: The seed is the word of God; the soil is the human heart.
Good soil hears the word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience.
Jeremiah: those who seek God with all their heart will find him.
q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart.
But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again each evening this week and keep one word in your heart.

sub: Micah was filled with the spirit of the Lord to speak truth with courage.
St Paul names the fruit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.
q: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately each day this week.

points.h: Bread that endures and a plan for each life
sub: Jesus urges us to work for the food that endures for eternal life.
God has plans for our welfare, a future with hope: every life has a vocation.
The Spirit leads young people to discover their call: priesthood, religious life, marriage.
q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.
points.apply: Pray for vocations, and encourage a young person to listen to God's call.

concl: The Spirit sows, nourishes and makes us fruitful.
Let us be good soil, bear his fruit, and feed on the bread that endures.
2027-05-23.resolve: Each night this week, examine: which fruit of the Spirit did I show today?

intro: Theme: “Called after a night of prayer.”

Jesus spends the night in prayer, chooses the Twelve, and proclaims the Beatitudes. The Spirit poured out at Pentecost makes this way of life possible for all of us: chosen, blessed, and called to holiness.

sub: Jesus spends the whole night in prayer before choosing the apostles.
He calls each by name and names them apostles, “sent ones”.
As God was with David, so he is with those he calls.
q: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD, the God of hosts, was with him.
Now during those days he went out to the mountain to pray; and he spent the night in prayer to God. And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles.
points.apply: Before an important decision this week, spend extra time in prayer.

sub: Jesus calls the poor, the hungry and those who weep “blessed”.
Their hope is in the kingdom that God promised, a kingdom that will never be destroyed.
The Beatitudes turn the world's values upside down.
q: For he is the living God, enduring forever. His kingdom shall never be destroyed, and his dominion has no end.
Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
points.apply: Thank God for one blessing hidden in a present difficulty.

points.h: Be holy: the cross and the cup of water
sub: God's command to Israel: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
Holiness means taking up the cross and following Jesus.
It also means small kindnesses: even a cup of cold water given in his name.
q: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
Whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones in the name of a disciple—truly I tell you, none of these will lose their reward.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of kindness each day this week.

concl: Prayer, poverty of spirit and humble love are the marks of those whom Christ calls.
Let the Spirit of Pentecost make us holy in great crosses and small kindnesses.
2027-05-30.resolve: Read the Beatitudes (Luke 6:20–26) each morning this week.
